description: Reviewed expected entailment labels for StarView connection explanations; model judgments are not mathematical proof.

cases.name: root-angle formula
cases.claim: The nth-root angles are obtained by dividing an argument plus integer multiples of two pi by n.

cases.name: invented Rouche bridge
cases.claim: The nth-root formula applies the argument principle and Rouchés theorem to count and locate polynomial roots.

cases.name: wrong complex graph description
cases.claim: The graph of a complex polynomial intersects the origin in the complex plane at a root.
cases.quote: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has at least one complex root.

cases.name: analyticity needs an open domain
cases.claim: Analyticity on a domain requires a complex derivative at every point of the open domain.
cases.quote: A function $f:D\to\mathbb C$ on an open set $D$ is called analytic on $D$ (or holomorphic on $D$) if $f\x27(z)$ exists at every point $z\in D$.

cases.name: nonzero derivative condition omitted
cases.claim: Every analytic function preserves angles at every point, including at critical points.
cases.quote: If the derivative is nonzero, its argument gives local rotation and its modulus gives local scaling.

cases.name: topology uses disks
cases.claim: A set is open when each of its points has a disk centered there that stays inside the set.
cases.quote: The set S is open if every point of S is an interior point. A point is interior if there exists r greater than zero such that D(z0,r) is contained in S.
